definitions.definition: A computer program that checks if a mathematical statement is proven correctly by following every logical step.
definitions.example: Like a spell-checker for math proofs.

definitions.definition: When a computer program is translated into machine code and checked for errors without any missing parts.
definitions.example: Like a teacher checking that every step of your homework is done before giving a grade.

definitions.definition: A placeholder in Lean that means 'I haven't proved this part yet' — like leaving a blank in a proof.
definitions.example: Like writing 'I'll finish this later' on a test question.

definitions.definition: A command in Lean that tells the computer to accept a statement as true without proof — like assuming something is true.
definitions.example: Like saying 'just trust me' in a math proof.

definitions.definition: A proof where every single step has been checked by a computer and nothing is missing.
definitions.example: Like a puzzle where every piece is in place and verified.

definitions.definition: Relating to the way parts are arranged or connected, not the specific details.
definitions.example: Like the frame of a house — the walls and roof are structural, the paint color is not.

definitions.definition: Information that comes from observation or experiments, not just theory.
definitions.example: Like measuring the temperature outside instead of guessing.

definitions.definition: A check that looks at two sides (like physics and theology) to see if they match up.
definitions.example: Like comparing two maps of the same city to see if they agree.

definitions.definition: A formal discussion or conversation about a topic.
definitions.example: Like a debate in class about a book.

definitions.definition: Something that a computer can verify automatically.
definitions.example: Like a computer checking if your password is correct.

definitions.definition: Able to be tested by trying to break it or find flaws, like a hacker testing security.
definitions.example: Like a friend trying to find mistakes in your argument on purpose.

definitions.definition: Specific rules that, if broken, mean the whole idea is wrong — like a 'game over' condition.
definitions.example: Like in a video game, if you lose all your health, the game ends.

definitions.definition: The idea that only one field (like science) is allowed to be strict and precise.
definitions.example: Like saying only math can be exact, but not art.

definitions.definition: A perfect one-to-one mapping between two structures that preserves all relationships.
definitions.example: Like two different maps of the same city that show the same streets and connections.

definitions.definition: A type of number that extends complex numbers, used to describe rotations in 3D space.
definitions.example: Like a special tool for spinning objects in computer graphics.

definitions.definition: A physical field that carries electric and magnetic forces, like around a magnet or wire.
definitions.example: Like the invisible force that makes a compass needle point north.

definitions.definition: The Christian idea of God as three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit) in one being, based on the Nicene Creed.
definitions.example: Like a family where three people are distinct but share the same family name.

definitions.definition: Results that look correct but are actually wrong — like a test saying you have a disease when you don't.
definitions.example: Like a fire alarm that goes off when there's no fire.

definitions.definition: A part that is essential for the whole structure to work — if removed, everything collapses.
definitions.example: Like the main pillar holding up a roof.

definitions.definition: A property that stays the same when two things are connected, even if other things change.
definitions.example: Like the total amount of money in two bank accounts stays the same when you transfer money between them.

definitions.definition: A way of combining a number (scalar) with a direction (vector) in physics equations.
definitions.example: Like combining speed (a number) with direction to get velocity.

definitions.definition: Using only quantities that have both size and direction, without separate numbers.
definitions.example: Like using only arrows, not plain numbers.

definitions.definition: The belief that God is one person who appears in different modes (like Father, Son, Spirit) but is not three distinct persons.
definitions.example: Like an actor playing three different roles, but being the same person.

definitions.definition: The idea that each person in the Trinity is a separate 'who' with their own relationships, not just a different role.
definitions.example: Like three friends who are different people, not one person wearing different hats.

definitions.definition: A three-part system where the parts interact and change over time.
definitions.example: Like a three-person team where each member's role changes based on the situation.

definitions.definition: The specific jobs or functions that each part of a system has.
definitions.example: Like in a sports team, each player has a position (goalie, forward, etc.).

definitions.definition: A detailed description of what something must do or be.
definitions.example: Like a recipe that lists exactly what ingredients and steps are needed.

definitions.definition: A proof method that checks every possible option and shows only one works.
definitions.example: Like trying every key on a key ring to find the one that opens a lock.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: When multiple things come together to a single point or result.
definitions.example: Like several roads meeting at a roundabout.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: Fairness where the punishment fits the crime — not too harsh or too lenient.
definitions.example: Like getting a detention for being late, not expelled.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: Treating everyone the same without favoritism.
definitions.example: Like a referee who calls fouls on both teams equally.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: Making things right for the person who was harmed.
definitions.example: Like someone who breaks a window paying to fix it.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: Choosing to take on a burden or pay a price willingly, not being forced.
definitions.example: Like volunteering to help a friend move instead of being told to.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: Applying to everyone, everywhere, without exception.
definitions.example: Like the rule 'don't steal' applies to all people.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: The idea that forgiveness is easy and costs nothing, without real change or responsibility.
definitions.example: Like saying 'sorry' but not meaning it or fixing the problem.
definitions.first_appearance: The Cross Is the Unique Solution

definitions.definition: The basic underlying layer or foundation that everything else is built on.
definitions.example: Like the ground under a building.

definitions.definition: Relating to the nature of reality beyond what we can see or measure.
definitions.example: Like asking 'what is real?' or 'does God exist?'

definitions.definition: The quality of being logically consistent and fitting together well.
definitions.example: Like a story where all the details make sense together.

definitions.definition: A system where parts are multiplied together, so if one part is zero, the whole result is zero.
definitions.example: Like a chain: if one link breaks, the whole chain fails.

definitions.definition: A system where scores are added up, so a weakness in one area can be balanced by strength in another.
definitions.example: Like a test where you can get a low score on one question but still pass if you do well on others.

definitions.definition: A standard way to match variables from one system to another.
definitions.example: Like a translation dictionary that maps words from English to Spanish.

definitions.definition: Not belonging to any specific field; works the same in different areas.
definitions.example: Like the number 2, which is the same in math, physics, and cooking.

definitions.definition: The limits or edges of a system that affect how it behaves.
definitions.example: Like the walls of a pool that determine how water moves.

definitions.definition: A person's overall way of understanding the world, including their beliefs and values.
definitions.example: Like seeing the world through a certain lens — scientific, religious, etc.

definitions.definition: An extra level of checking that looks at the type or meaning of something, not just its value.
definitions.example: Like checking not just that a package weighs 5 pounds, but that it's labeled 'fragile'.

definitions.definition: Swapping two things that have different meanings but look similar in a calculation.
definitions.example: Like swapping 'salt' and 'sugar' in a recipe — they look the same but taste different.

definitions.definition: A limit or test designed to catch mistakes or attacks.
definitions.example: Like a security checkpoint that checks for fake IDs.

definitions.definition: A check by experts in a specific field to see if something is correct.
definitions.example: Like having a doctor review a medical article.

definitions.definition: The weight of guilt or responsibility for doing wrong.
definitions.example: Like feeling guilty after lying to a friend.

definitions.definition: The Christian idea that Jesus Christ changes a person's moral state from guilty to forgiven.
definitions.example: Like having a debt paid by someone else.

definitions.definition: Existing first or being more fundamental in reality.
definitions.example: Like saying a tree exists before its shadow.

definitions.definition: Something that depends on another thing for its existence, like a parasite on a host.
definitions.example: Like a lie that twists the truth — it needs truth to exist.

definitions.definition: Existing first only by chance or circumstance, not necessarily.
definitions.example: Like being first in line because you arrived early, not because you're the leader.

definitions.definition: Having the same arrangement or pattern, even if the parts look different.
definitions.example: Like two different puzzles that have the same shape but different pictures.

definitions.definition: The Christian belief that God became human in the person of Jesus Christ.
definitions.example: Like a king becoming a commoner to live among the people.

definitions.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system; things tend to become more disordered over time.
definitions.example: Like a room getting messier if you don't clean it.

definitions.definition: The information or experience of having died, carried forward.
definitions.example: Like a scar that shows you were injured, even after you heal.

definitions.definition: The state of Jesus Christ before becoming human.
definitions.example: Like a person before they are born.

definitions.definition: Bringing someone back to life after they have stopped breathing or their heart has stopped.
definitions.example: Like CPR reviving a drowning person.

definitions.definition: Returning something to its original state, like restarting a computer.
definitions.example: Like erasing a drawing and starting over on a blank page.

definitions.definition: A base made of two different layers or materials that work together.
definitions.example: Like a road built on both gravel and asphalt.

definitions.definition: The way two systems are connected or linked together.
definitions.example: Like two gears that are meshed together.

definitions.definition: A condition that prevents a process from going backward.
definitions.example: Like an egg that can't be un-scrambled.

definitions.definition: A mathematical product (multiplication) of all factors that determines overall coherence.
definitions.example: Like a final score that is the product of several test scores.

definitions.definition: A design where if any single part is zero, the whole system fails.
definitions.example: Like a chain where one broken link makes the whole chain useless.

definitions.definition: A table or grid that shows how two domains (like physics and theology) connect.
definitions.example: Like a translation table between two languages.

definitions.definition: Standard, accepted connections between two domains.
definitions.example: Like official translations in a dictionary.

definitions.definition: A property that stays the same even when you change the context or field.
definitions.example: Like the number 2 being the same in math and physics.

definitions.definition: A standard, agreed-upon way to match elements from one set to another.
definitions.example: Like a standard conversion chart from inches to centimeters.

definitions.definition: Proofs that show if a certain condition is met, the whole system fails.
definitions.example: Like showing that if one ingredient is missing, the recipe fails.

definitions.definition: A mapping that preserves both the basic structure and the way parts change or interact.
definitions.example: Like a map that shows both the streets and the traffic rules.

definitions.definition: Testing by deliberately trying to create wrong results that look correct.
definitions.example: Like a hacker trying to break into a system to find weaknesses.

definitions.definition: A detailed description of how parts are arranged and connected.
definitions.example: Like a blueprint for a building showing where walls and doors go.

definitions.definition: A series of rules or checks that must be followed in order.
definitions.example: Like a checklist that must be completed step by step.
